title: iOS Metal Gaussian-splat render de-risk (depth sort + on-device 30 fps)
summary: Retire the #1 program risk: render a reconstructed Gaussian splat correctly, depth-sorted, at 30 fps on a physical iPhone in Unity 6 URP. Trainer-orthogonal — the failure is Unity's per-frame Metal depth sort (aras-p radix sort glitches on Metal, issue #226). Plan in design/proposals/ios-splat-render-v1.md: baseline aras-p (MIT) on desktop, then fix the Metal sort with a tile-local bitonic sort (msplat approach) or a native Metal plugin wrapping MetalSplatter (MIT); hold splats to ~1-2.5M via gsplat MCMC + SOG/.spz. Render-path-first (Owner decision, AUTH #030 spike).
deliverables: unity/ (splat render integration + iOS Metal sort fix or native plugin)

acceptance_tests.test: aras-p/UnityGaussianSplatting (MIT) is integrated in Unity 6 URP via GaussianSplatURPFeature (render graph, Compatibility Mode off) and renders a corpus splat correctly in the Editor/desktop as the baseline.

On a physical iPhone, splats render with correct back-to-front depth ordering (no glitching) using the chosen Metal sort fix — a tile-local bitonic sort (Option A) or a native Metal plugin wrapping MetalSplatter (Option B). This is the gate for 'solved'.

At a room splat budget (~1-2.5M, gsplat MCMC), sustained frame rate and package size are recorded against the 30 fps and <=150 MB targets, with SOG/.spz compression. Measurements are suggested evidence (SPEC §11), not a gate.
An LOD / chunked-streaming approach is specified (aras-p has none) so larger or multi-room scenes stay within budget on device.
The renderer loads splats only through signed, short-lived URLs (SECURITY_CHECKLIST §3.1), never a direct storage URL.

history.event: created by the Builder as the render-first spike track (the #1 program risk, orthogonal to the trainer). Plan in design/proposals/ios-splat-render-v1.md; complements M0-UNITY-02 (general renderer) and M1-CAPT-03 (produces the splat).
